mcqs.question: A solid cylindrical rod of length 20 cm and radius 2 cm is melted and recast into a solid cube. Which of the following statements about the resulting cube is correct?

options.A: The side length of the cube is (80π)^(1/3) cm.
options.B: The side length of the cube is 20 cm.
options.C: The side length of the cube is 2 cm.
options.D: The side length of the cube is (40π)^(1/3) cm.

mcqs.answer: The side length of the cube is (80π)^(1/3) cm.
mcqs.explanation: The volume of the cylinder is V=πr^2h=π·(2)^2·20=80π cm³. When melted, this volume becomes the volume of the cube, a^3. Hence a = (80π)^(1/3) cm. Options B, C and D do not satisfy the volume equality.

mcqs.question: A wooden block with volume 5000 cm³ is melted and recast into a solid sphere. What is the radius of the sphere (in cm) correct to two decimal places?
mcqs.explanation: For a sphere, V=4/3πr³. Setting 4/3πr³=5000 gives r³= (5000·3)/(4π)=15000/(4π)≈1193.66, so r≈10.50 cm. Only option B matches this value.

mcqs.question: A solid cube of side 4 cm is melted and recast into a cylinder whose height equals the side of the original cube. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The radius of the cylinder is √(16/π) cm.
options.B: The radius of the cylinder is 4 cm because surface areas are equal.
options.C: The radius of the cylinder is 2 cm because the height is halved.
options.D: The radius of the cylinder is 1 cm because volumes are equal.

mcqs.answer: The radius of the cylinder is √(16/π) cm.
mcqs.explanation: Volume of cube = 4³ = 64 cm³. Cylinder volume = πr²h with h=4 cm, so πr²·4 = 64 ⇒ r² = 16/π ⇒ r = √(16/π) cm. Options B, C, D use incorrect principles (surface area or wrong height).

mcqs.question: A solid sphere of radius r cm is melted and recast into a cube of side 3 cm. What is the value of r (in cm)?
mcqs.explanation: Cube volume = 3³ = 27 cm³. Set equal to sphere volume: (4/3)πr³ = 27 ⇒ r³ = 27·3/(4π). Hence r = (27·3/(4π))^{1/3}. Only option A reflects this derivation.

mcqs.question: A metal block has a volume of 0.002 m³. It is melted and recast into a right circular cylinder of radius 5 cm. What should be the height of the cylinder (in cm)?
mcqs.explanation: Convert volume to cm³: 0.002 m³ = 0.002×10⁶ = 2000 cm³. Height h = V/(πr²) = 2000/(π·5²) = 2000/(25π) = 80/π cm. Other options correspond to incorrect arithmetic.

mcqs.question: A goldsmith has 1000 cm³ of gold. He can either make a solid cube or a solid sphere using all the gold. Which shape will have the larger surface area?

options.A: The cube will have larger surface area.
options.B: The sphere will have larger surface area.
options.C: Both will have equal surface area.
options.D: It depends on the temperature of the gold.

mcqs.answer: The cube will have larger surface area.
mcqs.explanation: Cube side = 1000^{1/3}=10 cm, surface area = 6·10²=600 cm². Sphere radius r = (3·1000/(4π))^{1/3}≈6.2 cm, surface area = 4πr²≈483 cm². Hence the cube’s surface area is larger. Options B, C, D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: When a solid object is melted and recast into another shape, which physical quantity remains unchanged?
mcqs.explanation: Melting and recasting does not create or destroy material; therefore the volume (and mass) stays the same. Surface area, height, and edge lengths generally change.

mcqs.question: A cube of side 5 cm is melted and recast into a right circular cylinder of radius 3 cm. What is the height of the cylinder (in cm)?
mcqs.explanation: Cube volume = 5³ = 125 cm³. Cylinder volume = πr²h = π·3²·h = 9πh. Equate: 9πh = 125 ⇒ h = 125/(9π) cm. Only option A satisfies this equation.
